extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent attorneys, policy makers and members of the public seeking an overview of the EU unitary patent and Unified Patent Court
extracted.subtask_description: Summarising the legal framework, procedural requirements, territorial scope, translation and fee rules, and court/jurisdiction arrangements for the European patent with unitary effect (the EU unitary patent) and the related Unified Patent Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unitary effect (definition and legal consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unitary effect means the patent has a common legal status throughout all the participating states, eliminating scenarios in which a patent may be invalidated by courts in one participating member state yet upheld by courts in another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When unitary effect is granted the patent has a single legal status across the participating Member States: infringement and revocation proceedings are conducted before the Unified Patent Court (UPC) and decisions have a uniform effect for the unitary patent in the participating member states as a whole. The unitary patent may only be limited, transferred or revoked, or lapse, in respect of all participating Member States (but licensing is possible for part of the unitary territory).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing to request unitary effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Unitary effect may be requested by the proprietor within one month of grant of a European patent, replacing validation of the European patent in the individual countries concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request is made directly at the EPO; unitary effect has retroactive effect from the date of grant. (Draft rules also state unitary effect will be registered only if the European patent has been granted with the same set of claims for all participating member states.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for same set of claims for registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Unitary effect would be registered only if the European patent has been granted with the same set of claims for all the participating member states in the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement applies irrespective of whether the unitary effect will apply to all of those states or only some; it ensures uniformity of the granted patent across the unitary territory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Territorial scope depends on UPC ratification
rubrics_metrics.description: Unitary patents extend only to those participating member states for which the UPC Agreement has entered into force at the time of registration of the unitary patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the regulations formally apply to all participating states, unitary effect of newly granted unitary patents will be available only for the subset of participating states where the UPC Agreement has entered into force at the time of registration; later ratifications do not automatically extend the territorial scope of already-registered unitary patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coexistence with national and non-participating-state patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The unitary patent may coexist with nationally enforceable patents ('classical' patents) in the non-participating states and does not cover EPC countries that are not EU members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon grant and registration of unitary effect, the 'national' European patents are retroactively considered to never have existed in territories where unitary effect applies; unitary patents do not affect national patents in states where unitary effect does not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified Patent Court (UPC) jurisdiction (exclusive and transitional)
rubrics_metrics.description: The UPC has exclusive jurisdiction in infringement and revocation proceedings involving European patents with unitary effect, and during a transition period non-exclusive jurisdiction regarding European patents without unitary effect in states where the Agreement applies, unless the patent proprietor decides to opt out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The UPC also has jurisdiction to hear appeals against certain decisions of the EPO regarding unitary patents. As a court of several member states it may or must ask prejudicial questions to the European Court of Justice on EU law matters (excluding the UPC Agreement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals and relationship between EPO decisions and UPC
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions of the European Patent Office regarding the unitary patent are open to appeal to the Unified Patent Court, rather than to the EPO Boards of Appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shifts review of some EPO-related decisions into the UPC judicial framework for unitary patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the European Patent Office (administrative tasks)
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO performs certain administrative tasks authorised by Article 143(1) EPC, including the collection of renewal fees, registration of unitary effect upon grant, and recording licences and statements that licences are available to any person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal fees for the unitary patent are collected by the EPO; the EPO keeps 50% and redistributes the other 50% to the participating member states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirements (general rule and transitional arrangements)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a unitary patent, ultimately no translation will be required (except under certain circumstances in the event of a dispute). However, during a transitional period of minimum six years and no more than twelve years, one translation needs to be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the transitional period a full translation of the specification needs to be provided either into English if proceedings at the EPO were in French or German, or into any other EU official language if the proceedings were in English. Such translations are described as 'for information purposes only' and have no legal effect. Machine translations will also be provided 'for information purposes only.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations in legal proceedings (exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although translations are generally not required for unitary patents after the transition, translations may be required in the event of litigation or dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation provides for special translation arrangements in disputes so that parties/domestic courts can access a language version when needed; absence of such a translation can affect damages/knowledge in infringement scenarios under earlier proposals (and is handled in specific rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal/maintenance fee structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Unitary patent renewal fees are payable as a single renewal fee planned to be based on cumulative renewal fees due in the four countries where EPs were most often validated (Germany, France, UK, Netherlands).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fees were planned to range from 35 Euro in the second year to about 4,855 Euro in the 20th year (figures given as planned in the article). The EPO collects the fees and keeps 50% while redistributing 50% to participating states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost and expected savings (policy rationale and criticisms)
rubrics_metrics.description: The unitary patent system's stated aims are to make access to the patent system easier, less costly and legally secure within the EU, and to create uniform patent protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The European Commission estimated large cost savings versus validating in every EU country, but that estimate has been criticised as exaggerated; more realistic estimates suggest much smaller savings for the average patent validated in a few countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Object of property and applicable national law
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 7 of Regulation 1257/2012 provides that a European patent with unitary effect will be treated 'in its entirety and in all participating Member States as a national patent of the participating Member State in which that patent has unitary effect and in which the applicant had her/his residence or principal place of business or, by default, had a place of business on the date of filing the application.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant had no domicile in a participating Member State, German law will apply as the applicable national law for property aspects (per the regulation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and partial territorial licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensing is possible for part of the unitary territory despite the unitary patent being uniform across participating states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the unitary patent is unitary in property and enforcement, regulatory text explicitly allows licenses to cover part (not necessarily the whole) of the unitary territory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special territories inclusion/exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the unitary patent is introduced by an EU regulation it is expected to apply to special territories that are part of the European Union (a specified list), while other dependent territories may require national implementing legislation and therefore may not be covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article lists territories (e.g., Åland, French overseas departments, Büsingen am Hochrhein, etc.) expected to be covered; some overseas territories (e.g., French Polynesia, New Caledonia) are excluded until implementing legislation is passed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal basis and implementing instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: The unitary patent is implemented by three instruments: Regulation (EU) No 1257/2012, Council Regulation (EU) No 1260/2012 (translation arrangements), and the Agreement on a Unified Patent Court; it is based on EU law and the EPC (Article 142).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These instruments together form the 'unitary patent package' and define the legal/structural framework, including the translation rules, registration of unitary effect, and the UPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on 'bundle' character of European patents and centralized procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A European patent becomes a bundle of national patents upon grant; centralized opposition (within 9 months), limitation and revocation procedures remain centralized at the EPO, but enforcement is governed by national law unless unitary effect is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By requesting unitary effect, the proprietor obtains a unitary patent that replaces national validations in participating states and places enforcement and revocation before the UPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opt-out possibility during UPC transitional period
rubrics_metrics.description: During a transition period the UPC's jurisdiction regarding European patents without unitary effect is non-exclusive unless the patent proprietor decides to opt out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent proprietors may choose to keep their classical EPs outside UPC jurisdiction during the transitional phase by filing an opt-out, preserving national litigation routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of responsibilities and locations under UPC
rubrics_metrics.description: The UPC has a central division (Paris main seat, thematic branch in Munich, and a replaced London location), a Court of Appeal and registry seats in Luxembourg, and may have local/regional divisions in member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central division organization includes thematic clusters and the court may ask preliminary questions to the ECJ on EU law issues (excluding the UPC Agreement). The central division's arrangement split according to technology was part of the compromise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry into force mechanics and ratification consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Unitary patent system applies from the date the UPC Agreement enters into force; unitary effect for newly granted patents applies only to states for which the UPC Agreement has entered into force at the time of registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry into force was triggered by ratification sequences (e.g., Germany's deposit triggered the entry into force countdown); some states may sign/ratify later, but that does not retroactively extend unitary effect to already-registered patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine translations as information tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Machine translations will be provided and are explicitly described as 'for information purposes only' and should not have any legal effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of the translation arrangements intended to reduce costs and increase accessibility, but machine translations carry no legal weight for interpretation.
